target.title: fix(docs): expose top-level docs hubs on mobile
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users browsing the docs site on mobile cannot easily discover or navigate to the desktop top-level docs tabs when the mobile UI collapses the docs navigation.

On desktop, `https://docs.openclaw.ai/` exposes a horizontal top navigation bar with:

`Get started`, `Install`, `Channels`, `Agents`, `Capabilities`, `ClawHub`, `Models`, `Platforms`, `Gateway & Ops`, `Reference`, and `Help`.

On iPhone-sized mobile views, the horizontal top navigation is not visible. The visible mobile `Menu` button opens the current section sidebar only. On the docs home page, that means the user sees the `Get started` section pages (`OpenClaw`, `Showcase`, `Features`, first steps, guides), but not the full desktop tab list. This makes it hard for mobile users to find, or even know about, major docs areas such as `Install`, `Channels`, `Models`, `Platforms`, `Gateway & Ops`, and `Reference`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an early `Browse docs` hub section to the docs home page that mirrors the desktop top-level navigation as normal page content. It does not change the Mintlify navigation configuration or attempt to override Mintlify's mobile menu behavior; it gives mobile users an immediate in-page path to the same top-level docs areas.

## User Impact

Mobile users now get direct, visible links to the major docs areas near the top of the docs home page, even when the mobile menu only exposes the current section sidebar.

## Evidence

Screenshots are kept as PR evidence links instead of product-repo assets. The
links below point to the earlier non-merged fork commit that captured the proof
images; the final PR tree does not add these PNGs.

Desktop docs view: the horizontal top nav is visible and includes the full tab list.

![Desktop docs top navigation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bdjben/openclaw/d1c03771d5596259a289ea36cf90a1458f6f16da/docs/assets/mobile-navigation-evidence/desktop-docs-top-nav.png)

iOS Safari / iPhone 17 Pro Simulator at normal mobile zoom: the desktop horizontal nav is absent from the initial mobile UI. The page shows a `Menu` button, language selector, theme toggle, search, and page content.

![iOS Safari docs home mobile view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bdjben/openclaw/d1c03771d5596259a289ea36cf90a1458f6f16da/docs/assets/mobile-navigation-evidence/ios-safari-docs-home.png)

Mobile-width menu open: the menu opens the current `Get started` sidebar, not the desktop top-level tab list.

![Mobile menu shows current section only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bdjben/openclaw/d1c03771d5596259a289ea36cf90a1458f6f16da/docs/assets/mobile-navigation-evidence/mobile-menu-open.png)

Verification performed:

- Reproduced the live desktop docs UI at `https://docs.openclaw.ai/` with OpenClaw Browser and Puppeteer at `1440x1000`.
- Reproduced the iOS mobile view in the iPhone 17 Pro Simulator running Safari on iOS 26.5.
- Reproduced the opened mobile menu with an iPhone-sized mobile viewport and Safari user agent.
- Confirmed `docs/docs.json` defines the desktop tabs under `navigation.languages[0].tabs`.
- Confirmed the new section links to the same top-level docs areas exposed by the desktop nav.

Checks:

- `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check` passed locally.
- GitHub Actions `check-docs` passed after refreshing `docs/docs_map.md`.
- GitHub Actions `actionlint`, `no-tabs`, `preflight`, `security-fast`, `security-sensitive-guard`, and `Real behavior proof` passed on the previous clean run.
